stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architecture, and the AI community.

stories.title: Google Assistant will disappear from your phone next month
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Google is deprecating Google Assistant across Android phones, tablets, and paired devices.
The removal is directly linked to the integration and rise of Gemini.
The official cutoff date for Assistant access is set for September 4th.

stories.title: SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to build a terrestrial mobile network.
The goal is to directly compete with major US carriers (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon).
The announcement was made by Elon Musk and Gwynne Shotwell during a recent earnings call.

stories.title: AMD’s data center business is booming while gaming takes a backseat
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: AMD's data center revenue has experienced massive growth, more than doubling year-over-year.
The surge is directly attributed to high demand for AI computing capacity.
This growth highlights a significant industry shift favoring data center/AI infrastructure over traditional gaming segments for AMD.

stories.title: SpaceX made more revenue as an AI company than a space company
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: SpaceX's AI revenue has seen a significant surge, growing over threefold to $2.6 billion.
The primary driver for this AI revenue growth is providing compute services to other AI companies.
This indicates a major strategic shift, positioning SpaceX as a significant player in the AI infrastructure market.

stories.title: Texas halts data center connections to power grid amid overwhelming demand
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Texas is pausing data center connections to the power grid due to overwhelming demand.
This action directly contradicts previous claims by the Governor positioning Texas as an AI 'epicenter'.
The story highlights critical infrastructure limitations (power supply) impacting the growth of the AI industry.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in language modeling.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting accessibility within the current AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, currently serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these AI agents to run locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Mac devices.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs on the user's own device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
stories.author: Feng Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), a multimodal agent designed to process continuous video streams, moving beyond static image analysis.
Identifies two key limitations in current multimodal agents: modality bias (over-reliance on text search) and parametric knowledge leakage (over-reliance on internal memory).
Aims to improve agent performance by demanding dense spatiotemporal grounding and integrating open-web exploration capabilities.

stories.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
stories.author: Wenwei Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ParVL, a new scaling framework specifically designed for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
Addresses limitations in current MLLM scaling by moving beyond simple parameter or sequential inference expansion.
Key innovation is enabling flexible, task-specific allocation of compute resources between the Vision Transformer and LLM components.

stories.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
stories.author: Zhangyang Qi
bullet_points: Introduces SocietyBench, a new benchmark to evaluate LLMs' ability to forecast real-world social and world events.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation, which heavily focuses on task completion (e.g., coding, GUI operation) rather than social understanding.
The benchmark aggregates and analyzes web news and social media posts across five platforms based on a single event topic.

stories.title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
stories.author: Zhangyang Qi
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, prospective evaluation method for frontier LLMs, moving beyond traditional retrospective benchmarking.
Tests six advanced LLMs with web search capabilities by asking them to make real-time, match-by-match predictions during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Addresses the critical issue of LLM memorization in forecasting benchmarks by evaluating models on live, unfolding events.

stories.title: Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation
stories.author: riadsila
bullet_points: Mistral has released Shieldstral, a new 3B open-weights model.
The model is specifically designed for multimodal moderation tasks.
This contributes to the growing trend of open-source models in AI safety and content filtering.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces enhanced performance and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for improved functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval features.

stories.title: Disney gives TikTok creators official access to Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar characters
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Disney is integrating curated fan-created TikTok content directly into its Disney Plus app.
This move represents Disney's strategic effort to compete within the short-form video creator market.
The partnership leverages popular intellectual properties like Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar.

stories.title: Trump’s AI testing plan is limited and vague
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The Trump administration's AI cybersecurity risk assessment framework is reportedly limited and vague.
The framework explicitly excludes testing open-source AI models, which are publicly inspectable.
This exclusion suggests a potential bias or narrow focus within the administration's approach to AI regulation.

stories.title: Now you can securely link multiple phones to one Signal account
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Signal now allows users to securely link multiple mobile phones to a single account.
This update extends device linking beyond existing support for PCs and iPads.
Users can now check and respond to messages across all linked devices simultaneously.

stories.title: EA is now a private company
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Electronic Arts (EA) has successfully transitioned from a public to a private company.
The privatization deal was valued at $55 billion.
Key investors include Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners.

stories.title: Trump killed the Digital Equity Act, but US was forced to bring part of it back
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The Digital Equity Act program, valued at $1.25 billion, was partially restored despite initial political opposition.
A judicial ruling struck down the race-based provisions of the legislation as unconstitutional.
The story highlights a significant intersection of technology policy (digital equity) and legal/political maneuvering.

stories.title: China is Tesla's cash cow, but for how much longer?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla's Shanghai factory is experiencing high operational volume.
There is growing uncertainty regarding the long-term reliance on the Chinese market for Tesla's revenue.
The article suggests a potential strategic shift or decoupling from the Chinese market.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
stories.author: Jamie John, Financial Times
bullet_points: OpenAI publicly criticized Apple's lawsuit regarding trade secrets.
OpenAI stated they neither possess nor desire Apple's proprietary information.
The dispute highlights growing legal tensions between major AI developers and established tech giants.

stories.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Introduces 'TurnSight,' a new method for self-distillation designed to improve Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR) in LLMs.
Addresses the limitation of trajectory-level supervision in TIR, which hinders fine-grained credit assignment in long tasks.
Proposes using teacher branches with privileged context to generate denser training signals, moving beyond reliance on ground-truth answers.

stories.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: Test-time scaling allows LLMs to solve harder reasoning problems by increasing inference-time compute.
The concept encompasses diverse inference algorithms, including trajectory extension, candidate sampling/voting, and state search.
These different scaling procedures vary significantly in their statistical structure, compute accounting, and failure modes.

stories.title: Can Large Language Models Recover Semantic Optimization Opportunities That Compilers Miss?
stories.author: Chunwei Xia
bullet_points: The research investigates if Large Language Models (LLMs) can recover semantic optimization opportunities that traditional compilers fail to find.
The core problem addressed is that compilers miss optimizations when necessary semantics are missing from the program representation.
The authors introduce SeGaBench, a benchmark suite to test LLMs' ability to realize these recovered semantics as validated, contract-preserving code.

stories.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Introduces ReflectRL, a new method to improve LLM reasoning capabilities.
Addresses the issue where standard trajectory-guided methods discard 'failed' expert trajectories.
Proposes utilizing these 'Golden Negative Trajectories' as valuable negative supervision signals during training.

stories.title: Should We Type or Talk to LLM Agents? A Comprehensive Study of Voice and Keyboard Input Perturbations
stories.author: Jesse Thomason
bullet_points: The study investigates how different human input methods (typing vs. speaking) affect Large Language Model (LLM) performance.
It introduces HIVE, a tool designed to simulate and apply specific input perturbations, such as orthographic noise (keyboard) and disfluency (voice transcription).
The core goal is to evaluate the robustness of LLMs when faced with real-world variations in user input.

stories.title: Separating quantum circuits from classical LLMs
stories.author: Rik Sengupta
bullet_points: The research proves unconditional separations between low-depth quantum circuits and classical LLM architectures (transformers/diffusion models).
The separation is demonstrated in both the prediction and generation regimes of language models.
A specific distributional separation is shown, where a distribution is sampleable by constant-depth quantum circuits ($	extsf{QNC}^0$) but not by the classical models.

stories.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling
stories.author: Ali Jannesari
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inefficiency of fixed compute budgets in LLM test-time scaling.
It introduces 'adaptive test-time scaling' using a lightweight fuzzy controller.
This controller uses interpretable signals, like estimated prompt complexity, to allocate resources dynamically.

stories.title: A game theory for foundation models shows new paths to rational cooperation through similarity inference
stories.author: Blaise Agüera y Arcas
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new game theory framework to model the collective behavior of foundation model-powered autonomous agents.
It addresses a limitation of classical game theory, which assumes 'decoupled agency,' by accounting for agents jointly predicting environmental and actor states.
The research aims to establish principles for rational cooperation among increasingly integrated AI agents in complex systems.

stories.title: TACT: Taxonomy-Aligned Post-Training for Pedagogically Adaptive English Tutoring
stories.author: Zixin Chen
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current LLM-based ESL tutors, which lack pedagogical adaptability beyond simple conversational fluency.
TACT proposes a method (Taxonomy-Aligned Post-Training) to integrate human-tutoring principles into LLM training for better adaptive support.
The work focuses on bridging the gap between established educational psychology and practical LLM application in language learning.

stories.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
stories.author: Vipin Chaudhary
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'test-time scaling' in Reasoning LLMs, showing that increased inference-time compute improves problem-solving ability.
Test-time scaling encompasses diverse inference algorithms, including trajectory extension, candidate sampling/voting, and state searching.
The research highlights that these different inference procedures have distinct statistical structures, compute accounting methods, and failure modes.

stories.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
stories.author: Marco Valentino
bullet_points: The paper proposes pre-pretraining Language Models (LMs) on formal derivations (symbolic data) to enhance natural language acquisition.
Existing pre-pretraining methods are criticized for relying on narrow primitives that limit the models' ability to capture natural language's full expressive capacity.
The research aims to overcome limitations in prior studies, particularly concerning small token budgets, to better understand skill emergence in LMs.

stories.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment
stories.author: Peiqin Sun
bullet_points: Addresses the temporal credit-assignment challenge in aligning diffusion models with human preferences.
Introduces 'Latent Reward Registers' to estimate terminal preference directly from intermediate noisy latents.
Achieves this by prepending learnable, position-free register tokens to the input of a frozen Diffusion Transformer (DiT).

stories.title: PRISM: Powerful Time Series to Image (TS2I) Representations for Multivariate Anomaly Detection
stories.author: Roberto Corizzo
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of multivariate time series anomaly detection (TSAD) where representation choice is critical.
Proposes PRISM, a method that transforms time series data into image representations for anomaly detection.
Investigates the efficacy of using vision backbones (like those used in image processing) for time-domain anomaly detection tasks.

stories.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces PAST-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test recursive self-improvement in personal AI agents.
The research addresses the critical, yet untested, question of whether accumulated experience actually leads to improved future behavior in AI agents.
Personal AI agents are highlighted as a suitable setting for this study due to their ability to retain preferences, histories, and learned skills across sessions.

stories.title: Agogic: Performance-Timed Music Tokens for LLM-Native Text-to-Symbolic-Music Generation
stories.author: Ruqi Huang
bullet_points: The research introduces 'Agogic,' a method for performance-timed music tokens to improve LLM-native text-to-symbolic-music generation.
The study isolates the impact of music tokenization representation by systematically swapping representations across seven different tokenizations while keeping other model parameters fixed.
The findings suggest that the choice of representation, rather than the size of the underlying model (e.g., Qwen3.5), is the primary determinant of generation quality.

stories.title: When Attention Goes Blind: Numerical Failure in ALiBi Positional Encodings
stories.author: Gerhard Heyer
bullet_points: Identifies a critical, previously overlooked failure mode in ALiBi positional encodings.
The failure involves linear bias scaling underflowing floating-point precision, effectively zeroing out attention weights.
The research analyzes the impact and proposes four mitigation strategies for state-of-the-art models using ALiBi.

stories.title: HalluTruthQA-4K: A Fine-Grained Corpus and Annotation Process for Arabic Hallucination Detection and Truth Verification
stories.author: Abdenour Hadid
bullet_points: Introduces HalluTruthQA-4K, a new, expanded corpus for Arabic language processing.
Addresses the critical issue of factual errors (hallucinations) in Arabic LLM outputs.
Improves upon existing resources by providing fine-grained annotations, detailing the specific error and correct facts, rather than just binary labeling.

stories.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
stories.author: Marco Valentino
bullet_points: The research proposes pre-pretraining Language Models (LMs) using formal derivations (symbolic data) to enhance natural language acquisition.
Existing pre-pretraining methods are criticized for relying on narrow primitives that do not capture the full expressive capacity of natural language.
The study aims to address limitations in prior work by exploring skill emergence and representational dynamics over larger token budgets.

stories.title: rust-lang/rust is adopting an LLM policy
stories.author: blog.rust-lang.org via wezm
bullet_points: The Rust programming language community is implementing a formal policy regarding the use of Large Language Models (LLMs).
This indicates a growing need within major open-source ecosystems to define guidelines for AI integration and usage.
The adoption of such a policy is a moderate but significant shift in how established programming language projects manage modern tooling and AI.

stories.title: The Review Tax: Why 81% of Developers Are Buried in AI Code Review
stories.author: harsh2644
bullet_points: The article addresses the growing reliance on AI for code review in software development.
It highlights a concerning statistic: 81% of developers are reportedly overwhelmed by AI-generated code reviews.
The core theme warns against the potential dangers of blindly accepting AI-generated code.

stories.title: Who Is the Author? AI-Generated Code and PCI DSS Code Review
stories.author: yehyatt
bullet_points: The article addresses the conflict between AI-generated code and PCI DSS compliance requirements.
PCI DSS mandates that code reviews must be performed by an individual independent of the original code author.
The discussion centers on how AI-generated code complicates established security and compliance protocols.

stories.title: I type-check AI-generated SDK code against the real package. Claude refused a third of my Stripe tasks.
stories.author: kalpitrathore
bullet_points: A developer created 'SDKProof' to validate AI-generated SDK code against actual package implementations.
The tool highlights issues where large language models (like Claude) failed to produce correct code for complex tasks (e.g., Stripe integration).
The story addresses the current reliability and verification challenges when using AI agents for production-ready code.

stories.title: Shieldstral Introduces Policy-Adaptive Multimodal Safety Classification in a 3B Model
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: Shieldstral has released a new 3B-parameter model focused on safety classification.
The model features 'policy-adaptive' capabilities, suggesting dynamic safety evaluation.
It is designed to assess multimodal inputs, combining text with other data types for safety.
